content.content:
Fred,

I'm flying to LA tomorrow morning for the Griffin AGM and the Dentsu meeting, so can you take the send list for the Q4 investor update off my plate? It goes out the week after the Oct 14 board and I'll write the update itself on the plane.

Our existing investors are already on my own list. What I need from you is everyone from the bridge round who should get it, as of tonight, with the groups and details in the Q4 update send list doc so I know which paragraph each one gets. The draft update deck shows what each group gets. Get the new investors right, they'll look for their own check in it.

Please put it in your Q4 investor update folder, the README in that folder says how to name it. Then do what I put on the Existing Investor Update card in Trello. Once it's done reply here with how many firms and angels are in each group. I put Monday's review on your calendar so we can go through it together.

Robert asked about just sending it to everyone on the 2025 list. Let's not, only the people the doc says.

Thanks,
Leonard

content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2\", \"title\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\", \"name\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\", \"revisionId\": \"1b0d9b5d65\", \"createdTime\": \"2025-09-26T18:00:00Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2025-09-26T18:41:00Z\", \"text\": \"Q4 investor update - send list\\nLeonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.\\n\\nWho to look at\\nEvery name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.\\n\\nGroups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)\\nGo by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.\\nNew investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.\\nIn talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.\\nAwaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.\\nKeep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.\\nEveryone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.\\nPassed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.\\n\\\"Us\\\" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.\\nAccelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.\\n\\nBuild access\\nFor firms in talks: whether they can get the current internal build, TestFlight on iOS and the Play internal test track on Android, so the update can carry the right link. Write iOS only, Android only, iOS and Android, or none. The public store pages don't count. Arthur tracks the tester adds. Leave it blank for angels.\\n\\nSheet\\nOne row per firm or angel that gets the update, off-list firms with a call included: firm, group, amount (new investors and angels in talks), build access (firms in talks). The ones who stay off don't go in the sheet.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_3b9e61c04d7a52e8f1a6c2", "title": "Q4 investor update - send list", "name": "Q4 investor update - send list", "revisionId": "1b0d9b5d65", "createdTime": "2025-09-26T18:00:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-26T18:41:00Z", "text": "Q4 investor update - send list
Leonard, Sep 26. Existing investors are on my own list, this doc is only for the bridge round.

Who to look at
Every name on the 2025 game investor list, angels included. The list has a few names twice, and a repeated name is still one entry. Plus any firm not on the list that we've had a pitch call or meeting with since we kicked off the bridge on Sep 3. A call counts when it's on Fred's calendar, even if he couldn't make it; calls that never went on Fred's calendar don't. Investment talks only, strategic investors included: if we pitched them the bridge or an investment alongside a co-dev deal, they count even when co-dev or publishing was on the table too. Service or work-for-hire deals, banks (our SVB catch-ups), RFPs, publishing-only talks and calls with other engine companies don't.

Groups, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 (Pacific)
Go by what has happened since the Sep 3 kickoff, that day included. On the list, go only by the Latest Status notes (as of 09/11), which are all from this round, and they count as written: a note that they passed or don't do bridges is their no, and a note that we reached out is our outreach. The list's Status and comment columns, answers from earlier rounds and plans to reach out don't count.
New investor: signed a SAFE this round (see my note in #executives on what counts as signed). Put the amount on their row.
In talks: we've had a call or meeting with them this round (on Fred's calendar) and they haven't passed. Angels who've said yes but haven't signed go here too, with the amount they said yes to.
Awaiting reply: we reached out this round, no call yet and no no, even if they've written back.
Keep warm: they passed after we pitched them on a call or meeting this round.
Everyone else stays off: they passed without a call or meeting, or nothing from us since Sep 3.
Passed means they've told us no for this round. A no to our pitch that they sent Griffin or an advisor rather than us counts too. An advisor's own read on whether a firm invests isn't the firm's answer.
"Us" includes anyone who reached out or made an intro on our behalf (IH, Matthew, an advisor). Only outreach about the bridge counts, not RFP or partnership mail.
Accelerator programs like a16z speedrun are separate from the bridge. The interview counts as a call with that firm, but the program's decision and the feedback that comes with it aren't their answer on the bridge; that has to come on our bridge thread with them or in #bridge-pitch.

Build access

content.content: {"result":"{\"ok\": true, \"messages\": [{\"ts\": \"1759085550.967869\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"\\n<https://www.linkedin.com/posts/taewonyun_hello-linkedin-friends-help-me-find-someone-activity-7377888042545549313-ldtM?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_ios&rcm=ACoAAAJh-KABiEYRx6CSQG-T5CsCMIE5rn-YkEs>\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759085532.160589\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"I also noticed my friend [PERSON_NAME_25249] announcing his plan at ncsoft on LinkedIn \", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759085484.722089\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"I don\\u2019t think it\\u2019s happening for us. We will likely get a rejection letter later this week or next \", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1759085462.583969\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"I started to see people announcing their acceptance to speedrun from [USERNAME_1453] and the application deadline is closing 2 days \", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1758927000.205874\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"told Mattel we're passing on the Barbie RFP. since the kickoff that's only been an RFP conversation, we haven't pitched them the bridge\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1758829663.118739\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"not a big deal in grand scheme of things\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1758829656.142509\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"I also booked an earlier one way flight to LA - because I have savers fare with Alaska they didn\\u2019t change my flight. They said they can do the change 24 hours priori to flight only - I didn\\u2019t want to risk it. Worst case this meeting is gonna cost us an extra $250\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1758829580.899319\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"trying to see if the has some flexibility\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1758829572.162199\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"I\\u2019m trying to schedule time with tapnation but their game acquisition guys\\u2019 meeting slots are 2am-6:30am my local time\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1758829538.194319\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"pinged [USERNAME_0458] just now\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1758822451.332039\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Well, gaming is hard, the biz model is figured out, but getting on the right path with the right game is hard, and sometimes There are lots of people on the same path and because everyone is in it, everyone loses where as if There was just one title of a genre, it can be profitable\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0016_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1758817200.730591\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"correction on Play Ventures: the no I pasted here on the 15th was what they told Griffin, not us. that's why I said they never answered us. it's still their no for this round, the \\\"discussing\\\" Robert heard via Applovin doesn't change that\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1758811177.338159\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"I think in their case they want to fund us but not for this lol\", \"channel\": \"C096HFA5Z8W\", \"user\": \"EMPLOYEE_0038_SLACK_ID\"}, {\"ts\": \"1758811165.790799\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Hey Leonard,\\n\\nReally sorry for the delayed reply, we were away last week in Istanbul and it was tough to find time to sync internally. Thanks again for walking me through the updates with Harmony Games, I really enjoyed the conversation! I managed to catch up with the rest of the investment team and unfortunately, we won\\u2019t be joining this round.\\n\\nThat said, I want to say how much we respect what you\\u2019re building. The speed at which you\\u2019ve been able to stand up the Harmony Games Engine and move from Domino Delights to Zombie Match 3D is impressive, and it\\u2019s clear the team has the right mix of experience and execution chops. Ultimately, though, we don\\u2019t feel Harmony Games is the right fit for us at this stage. I managed to catch up with the rest of the investment team and unfortunately, we won’t be joining this round.

That said, I want to say how much we respect what you’re building. The speed at which you’ve been able to stand up the Harmony Games Engine and move from Domino Delights to Zombie Match 3D is impressive, and it’s clear the team has the right mix of experience and execution chops. Ultimately, though, we don’t feel Harmony Games is the right fit for us at this stage. The content and market risk around scaling a new puzzle IP in the current environment feels higher than we’re comfortable with. I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Most major ad networks, including Google AdMob, Meta Audience Network, and Unity Ads, have strict policies against *incentivized ad views* and artificial engagement.\\n*Potential Policy Violations*\\nHere\\u2019s how your idea could violate various ad network policies:\\n1. *Incentivized Ad engagement (Against AdMob & Most Networks)*\\n    \\u25e6 Google AdMob *explicitly prohibits* rewarding users for watching ads unless it\\u2019s a rewarded ad format tied to in-app content (e.g., extra lives, virtual currency).\\n    \\u25e6 Your model directly incentivizes users to watch ads for real-world payouts, which is *not allowed*.\\n2. *Artificial engagement / Invalid Traffic*\\n    \\u25e6 Ad networks analyze user engagement, and if they detect that people are watching ads only for money (not genuine interest), they may classify the traffic as *invalid* and withhold earnings.\\n    \\u25e6 Clicks, impressions, and video views *must be organic*\\u2014forcing or incentivizing views creates *low-value interactions*, which networks can penalize.\\n3. *Revenue Share / Arbitrage Concerns*\\n    \\u25e6 If you\\u2019re paying users a portion of ad revenue, some networks may see this as *ad arbitrage*\\u2014where the intent is not genuine app usage but merely generating ad views.\\n    \\u25e6 Networks like AdMob *ban ad revenue-sharing schemes* that exist solely to funnel money to users.\\n4. *Bot & Fraud Detection Risks*\\n    \\u25e6 Many ad networks use sophisticated fraud detection systems. If a large percentage of users are just watching ads to earn money, it could trigger *fraud flags* and get your account banned.\\n    \\u25e6 Even if users are real, networks might still mark their engagement as *low-quality traffic* and *suspend payments*.\\n*Workarounds (If You Still Want Something Similar)*\\nIf you still want a reward-based system, consider these alternatives:\\n1. *Use a Legitimate Rewarded Ad Model*\\n    \\u25e6 AdMob, Unity, and other networks allow *rewarded ads* as long as the rewards stay within the app (e.g., coins, extra lives).\\n    \\u25e6 You could design a game where *watching ads enhances gameplay* rather than directly giving real-world cash.\\n2. *Partner with Alternative Ad Networks*\\n    \\u25e6 Some alternative ad networks (like Mistplay or OfferToro) specialize in *reward-based advertising*, but they typically *don\\u2019t allow direct ad revenue sharing*.\\n    \\u25e6 Look into *GPT (Get Paid To) networks* that allow users to complete offers, surveys, and ad views for rewards *without violating policies*.\\n3. *Use Affiliate or Direct Sponsorships Instead*\\n    \\u25e6 Instead of using standard ad networks, you could *partner with brands directly* and give users a cut of *affiliate revenue* (e.g., watching sponsored videos, completing brand challenges).\\n*Bottom Line*\\nYour current idea *will likely violate policies* and could get you *banned from major ad networks*. • You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. • There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

mkdir -p /app/tools; cat > /app/tools/dec.py <<'EOF'
import json,sys,base64,re
def b64(s):
    s=s.replace('-','+').replace('_','/'); s+='='*(-len(s)%4)
    return base64.b64decode(s).decode('utf-8','replace')
def body(p):
    out=[]
    if p.get('mimeType','').startswith('text/plain') and p.get('body',{}).get('data'):
        out.append(b64(p['body']['data']))
    for c in p.get('parts',[]) or []:
        out+=body(c)
    if not out and p.get('mimeType','').startswith('text/html') and p.get('body',{}).get('data'):
        out.append(re.sub('<[^>]+>',' ',b64(p['body']['data'])))
    return out
raw=json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))['result'] if sys.argv[1].endswith('.txt') else open(sys.argv[1]).read()
d=json.loads(raw)
msgs=d.get('messages',[d])
since=sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv)>2 else '0'
maxc=int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv)>3 else 3000
for m in msgs:
    if int(m.get('internalDate',0))<int(since): continue
    h={x['name']:x['value'] for x in m['payload'].get('headers',[])}
    print('=====',h.get('Date'),'|',h.get('From'),'->',h.get('To'),'cc',h.get('Cc'),'|',h.get('Subject'))
    t='\n'.join(body(m['payload']))
    # strip quoted
    t=re.split(r'\nOn .{5,80}wrote:|\n_{10,}|\nFrom: ',t)[0]
    print(t[:maxc])
EOF

Hi [PERSON_NAME_2327],

Thanks for the playthrough and notes and super glad to hear you enjoyed the
core fast matching action! You are right: the core loop grabs attention and
can pull focus from the zombie layer at the top. We have been working on
that tension between board focus and combat awareness. Our observation is
that players tend to build resolution over time and can eventually handle
both layers. Our heavier players past level 150 lean into it, which is why
we expect a strong D30/D7 ratio (yet to be seen). In early levels
difficulty comes from building up that resolution and reaching your
click-per-minute potential. Once someone reaches their potential, we'll not
make the game more difficult by adding smaller items or adding more time
pressure like Match Factory does (the main cause for their long-term churn
we believe). Instead difficulty is gonna start to come from not
upgrading your items and not bringing the right combat equipment to the
battlefield.

In parallel, we are testing mode variations across a spectrum that might
lead to a pivot into core game if metrics fail us:
1- from auto-play boosters that cover clutch zombie moments so you can look
at zombies to strategize
2- a charge-meter booster that temporarily converts match-3 to single-tap
match (Boss mode, you can try the charge up today - game mode still WIP)
fire so players can tap without watching the board
3- to completely bot-driven modes (capybara style).

We will run these iterations as quickly as we can and keep what works
for the audience. Thank you for putting the time in - it's much appreciated
on our end.

Best,
Leonard

Hi [PERSON_NAME_2327],

Thanks for the playthrough and notes and super glad to hear you enjoyed the
core fast matching action! You are right: the core loop grabs attention and
can pull focus from the zombie layer at the top. We have been working on
that tension between board focus and combat awareness. Our observation is
that players tend to build resolution over time and can eventually handle
both layers. Our heavier players past level 150 lean into it, which is why
we expect a strong D30/D7 ratio (yet to be seen). In early levels
difficulty comes from building up that resolution and reaching your
click-per-minute potential. Once someone reaches their potential, we'll not
make the game more difficult by adding smaller items or adding more time
pressure like Match Factory does (the main cause for their long-term churn
we believe). Instead difficulty is gonna start to come from not
upgrading your items and not bringing the right combat equipment to the
battlefield.

In parallel, we are testing mode variations across a spectrum that might
lead to a pivot into core game if metrics fail us:
1- from auto-play boosters that cover clutch zombie moments so you can look
at zombies to strategize
2- a charge-meter booster that temporarily converts match-3 to single-tap
match (Boss mode, you can try the charge up today - game mode still WIP)
fire so players can tap without watching the board
3- to completely bot-driven modes (capybara style).

We will run these iterations as quickly as we can and keep what works
for the audience. Thank you for putting the time in - it's much appreciated
on our end.

Best,
Leonard

Hi PERSON_2173_NAME,

Hope you’ve been well. We are finally kicking off a $2.5M bridge focused on
our [SOURCE_ORG_0001] Engine, the foundation for reaching the KPIs efficiently. For
context, Zombie Match 3D is still in alpha and Domino Delights is pursuing
a publisher. As a pure consumer app, we know the metrics you care about
will take time to mature, so we may not be a perfect fit on product KPIs
today. That said, I believe we could still be attractive from a platform
perspective for GRx:

AI-native studio: Engine built with AI at the core of design, content
generation, liveops, analytics, and UA.
Real co-creation workflows: Designers and AI working together for 10x
content velocity with a lean team.
Near-term engine milestones: Unifying puzzle and liveops tooling,
automating level and difficulty pipelines, self-serve tools for designers,
and tighter instrumentation for rapid, reliable experiments.
Efficient execution: Senior global team, disciplined burn at about $100K
per month, rapid iteration and multiple shots on goal.

If this platform-first angle fits your thesis, we would be delighted to
grab 30–45 minutes this week or in the next two weeks. I can walk through
the engine roadmap, early KPI reads, and how the platform de-risks
retention and UA over time.

*Attachments and links:* our pitch deck, two short engine demos, and live
store builds below.

Hi PERSON_2173_NAME,

Great to hear from you. Yes, the engine has always been the core focus.
Mobile hits are inherently hit-or-miss, so our strategy is to create
multiple shots on goal. The engine lets a lean team stand up new concepts
quickly, iterate fast, and carry forward what works.

On cadence: 4-5 months is the right ballpark for getting a new title to
playable/soft launch if Zombie Match’s alpha metrics do not meet our
targets. If Zombie Match hits, we’ll double down and scale it. If it does
not, we’ll move the next title into the pipe without losing momentum.

We’re still very much a game studio at heart and aim to build the best
puzzle RPGs in the world. Longer term, the engine also opens up second- and
third-party opportunities, but near term our focus is our own titles.

Hope this helps. Let me know if you have any other questions.
Best regards,
Leonard

content.content:
===== Wed, 3 Sep 2025 14:09:34 -0700 | leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> -> PERSON_2173_NAME <PERSON_2173_EMAIL> cc frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> | Re: GRx Feedback
Hi PERSON_2173_NAME,

Hope you’ve been well. We are finally kicking off a $2.5M bridge focused on
our [SOURCE_ORG_0001] Engine, the foundation for reaching the KPIs efficiently. For
context, Zombie Match 3D is still in alpha and Domino Delights is pursuing
a publisher. As a pure consumer app, we know the metrics you care about
will take time to mature, so we may not be a perfect fit on product KPIs
today. That said, I believe we could still be attractive from a platform
perspective for GRx:

AI-native studio: Engine built with AI at the core of design, content
generation, liveops, analytics, and UA.
Real co-creation workflows: Designers and AI working together for 10x
content velocity with a lean team.
Near-term engine milestones: Unifying puzzle and liveops tooling,
automating level and difficulty pipelines, self-serve tools for designers,
and tighter instrumentation for rapid, reliable experiments.
Efficient execution: Senior global team, disciplined burn at about $100K
per month, rapid iteration and multiple shots on goal.

If this platform-first angle fits your thesis, we would be delighted to
grab 30–45 minutes this week or in the next two weeks. I can walk through
the engine roadmap, early KPI reads, and how the platform de-risks
retention and UA over time.

*Attachments and links:* our pitch deck, two short engine demos, and live
store builds below.

*Engine demos*
[SOURCE_ORG_0001] Puzzle Engine: https://youtu.be/kgcL7xexAAk
<https://youtu.be/kgcL7xexAAk?utm_source=ch
===== Thu, 4 Sep 2025 12:39:19 -0400 | PERSON_2173_NAME <PERSON_2173_EMAIL> -> leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> cc frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> | Re: GRx Feedback
Hi Leonard,

Thanks for reaching out, hope you've been well too!

I appreciate you sharing all of these updates and links with me. So
high-level if I'm understanding correctly, the engine is becoming the main
focus and the plan is to launch a new title every 4-5 months?

Thanks,
PERSON_2173_NAME
===== Thu, 4 Sep 2025 21:50:45 -0700 | leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> -> PERSON_2173_NAME <PERSON_2173_EMAIL> cc frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> | Re: GRx Feedback
Hi PERSON_2173_NAME,

Great to hear from you. Yes, the engine has always been the core focus.
Mobile hits are inherently hit-or-miss, so our strategy is to create
multiple shots on goal. The engine lets a lean team stand up new concepts
quickly, iterate fast, and carry forward what works.

On cadence: 4-5 months is the right ballpark for getting a new title to
playable/soft launch if Zombie Match’s alpha metrics do not meet our
targets. If Zombie Match hits, we’ll double down and scale it. If it does
not, we’ll move the next title into the pipe without losing momentum.

We’re still very much a game studio at heart and aim to build the best
puzzle RPGs in the world. Longer term, the engine also opens up second- and
third-party opportunities, but near term our focus is our own titles.

Hope this helps. Let me know if you have any other questions.
Best regards,
Leonard
===== Fri, 5 Sep 2025 08:28:33 -0400 | PERSON_2173_NAME <PERSON_2173_EMAIL> -> leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> cc frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> | Re: GRx Feedback
Thanks for clarifying! Let me have a chat with my team first (we do a
Monday investment team meeting) to run all the updates by them. I want to
be mindful of your time if the traction/metrics right now are going to be a
point of hesitation for my team.
===== Mon, 8 Sep 2025 09:41:31 -0400 | PERSON_2173_NAME <PERSON_2173_EMAIL> -> leonard hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co> cc frederick stone <frederick.stone@harmonygames.co>, robert <robert@harmonygames.co>, arthur blake <arthur.blake@harmonygames.co> | Re: GRx Feedback
Hi Leonard,

I was able to discuss with my team and share the updates with them,
unfortunately it would still be less of a fit for us to revisit a potential
investment right now. Generally speaking, my team is pretty
metrics-oriented, so even though There's an appreciation for what you're
doing on the engine side the game KPIs aren't There yet for my team to
build conviction around a potential investment. Hope that makes sense.

Thanks,
PERSON_2173_NAME

content.content: {"result":"{\"ok\": true, \"messages\": [{\"ts\": \"1759288987.503349\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"We got the expected rejection letter from A16Z - I think it\\u2019s very well-written response. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.\\n\\nLeonard and team,\\n\\nThanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It\\u2019s obvious this isn\\u2019t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you\\u2019ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.\\n\\nAfter reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we\\u2019ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it\\u2019s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:\\n\\nThere\\u2019s a lot to like about what you\\u2019re building:\\n\\u2022 You\\u2019ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don\\u2019t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There\\u2019s a clear rhythm to how you\\u2019re executing.\\n\\u2022 We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you\\u2019re building toward true scalability.\\n\\u2022 There\\u2019s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2\\u20133 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t\\u2019s clear you\\u2019re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.\\nWhat\\u2019s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We\\u2019d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.\\n\\nWe also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it\\u2019s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We\\u2019d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.\\n\\n\\nThis was a tough call. You\\u2019re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We\\u2019ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we\\u2019d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.\\n\\nThanks again for sharing the journey with us. {"ok": true, "messages": [{"ts": "1759288987.503349", "type": "message", "text": "We got the expected rejection letter from A16Z - I think it’s very well-written response. I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Leonard,

Done. The send list is in my Q4 2025 investor update folder as "Q4 update - send list" (Google Sheet, shared with you):
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/12r1wfEZMaHWHERuVYgls6RMeiNJAT4NRX_5UqpVX7hQ/edit

Counts, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 PT:
- New investor: 0 firms, 1 angel (Anton Bernstein, $25,000; his DocuSign Completed notice came in Sep 26)
- In talks: 7 firms, 0 angels (GFR Fund, a16z, Dentsu, T-Accelerate, NCsoft, Brightwater Games Fund, Homa)
- Awaiting reply: 14 firms, 0 angels
- Keep warm: 3 firms, 0 angels (LVP, Hiro Capital, SciPlay)
Total: 24 firms and 1 angel.

A few calls worth flagging for Monday:
- Paul Heydon is off. He told you Sep 30 he can't put money in this year, and we never had a call with him.
- SciPlay moved to Keep warm. D called Robert on Sep 30 to pass.
- a16z stays In talks. The speedrun interview counts as the call, but the speedrun rejection isn't their answer on the bridge.
- Build access: the 4 firms with links can only get iOS. Arthur found the Play investor tester list was never attached to the internal track, even though the Linear log says otherwise. So T-Accelerate, Dentsu, NCsoft and Brightwater are iOS only, and GFR, a16z and Homa have none yet.

On the Existing Investor Update card I added New investor, In talks, Awaiting reply and Keep warm checklists, one item per firm or angel. I also added 18 "F/up with..." cards in To Do. Dentsu (Oct 1) and Makers Fund (Oct 8) don't get one because they're already on my calendar. NCsoft got a comment on the existing "F/up with Anel" card instead of a new card.

See you Monday.

Fred

The send list is done, Leonard's Trello card is updated, and I've replied on his thread with the counts. It's all ready for the Oct 6 review.

**Groups (bridge round, as of end of day Tue Sep 30 Pacific)** — 24 firms and 1 angel:

| Group | Firms | Angels | Who |
|---|---|---|---|
| New investor | 0 | 1 | Anton Bernstein, $25,000 (DocuSign completed Sep 26) |
| In talks | 7 | 0 | GFR Fund, a16z, Dentsu, T-Accelerate, NCsoft, Brightwater Games Fund, Homa |
| Awaiting reply | 14 | 0 | Initial Capital, BITKRAFT, Makers Fund, Raine, General Catalyst, BBQ Capital, Treo VC, Superplay, Sony Mobile, Revo, e2vc, Triptyq, Turkven, Harlem Capital |
| Keep warm | 3 | 0 | LVP, Hiro Capital, SciPlay |

**What I did:**
- **Sheet:** "Q4 update - send list" is in your Q4 2025 investor update folder and shared with Leonard. It has one row per firm or angel with group, amount, build access and a short note on why each one landed where it did.
- **Trello:** I added New investor, In talks, Awaiting reply and Keep warm checklists to the Existing Investor Update card, one item each. The Keep warm checklist didn't exist yet, so I created it too.
- **Follow-up cards:** I made 18 "F/up with…" cards in To Do. Dentsu and Makers Fund don't get one because they already have meetings on your calendar after Sep 30 (Oct 1 and Oct 8). NCsoft already had a card ("F/up with Anel…"), so I commented on that instead.
- **Reply:** It went on Leonard's thread with these counts. Reply-all only went to Leonard, not Robert or Arthur. Forward it if they need it.

**Worth raising on Monday:**
- **Paul Heydon is off the list.** He told Leonard on Sep 30 he can't put money in this year, and there was never a call with him.
- **SciPlay is in Keep warm.** They passed by phone to Robert on Sep 30, after a call this round.
- **a16z is in In talks.** Their speedrun interview counts as a call, but the speedrun rejection isn't an answer on the bridge.
- **Build access:** Arthur posted that the Android investor tester list was never attached to the Play internal track, even though his Linear log says otherwise. I went with his Slack note: T-Accelerate, Dentsu, NCsoft and Brightwater have iOS only. GFR, a16z and Homa have no access yet.
- **Homa** isn't named on the calendar invite (Rohan Jain, Sep 18). I identified it from Slack, where Leonard listed "SciPlay and homa" as that week's calls.
- **Robert's suggestion** to send to everyone on the 2025 list wasn't followed, per Leonard's instruction.
